name: Revit Parameters (read and batch-set instance or type parameters)
description: Read and batch-set instance or type parameters of placed elements from data. revit_get_parameters is read-only: use it first to see names, units and which parameters are writable. revit_set_parameters is a write tool: it needs an approved plan, never creates parameters, refuses read-only and critical built-in ones per element, writes one transaction per element, reads every value back and returns old and new values plus a revert list. dry_run tries it and rolls it all back.
author: AEC Model Bridge

commands.title: Read parameter values of elements picked by id, ids or a selector (category, name, level, tag): one row per element and parameter with the value in the unit revit_set_parameters expects, Revit's display text, read-only, and whether revit_set_parameters would write it and why not. Leave params empty to list every parameter. Read-only; use it before revit_set_parameters. Capped by max_elements and a time budget; truncated says the list is not complete. For one element's raw record revit_get_element_parameters also works.

items.description: What to read (1 to 50 items): each item picks elements with exactly one of id, ids or selector, and names the parameters.

selector.description: Pick elements by properties instead of ids. Needs category or tag, so the whole model is never scanned; name and level narrow it.

category.description: Category name, for example Walls, Doors, Windows, Pipes or OST_GenericModel.

name.description: Exact element name (for a family instance this is its type name).

level.description: Exact name of the level the element is on.

tag.description: Prefix of the Comments parameter that marks the elements of one build phase.

scope.description: instance (default): the selected element itself (a type id also means that type). type: the element type of each selected element; instances that share a type count once.

params.description: Parameter names to read (at most 100). Empty or left out: every parameter of the element.

max_elements.description: Read at most this many elements (1 to 2000, default 200); more matches make the result partial.

time_budget_s.description: Stop reading after this many seconds (1 to 25, default 10) and return a partial result.

limit.description: Most rows to return (default 100, at most 500). The full list is written to a detail file when it is longer.

offset.description: Skip this many rows first, to read the next page of a truncated list.

count_only.description: Return only the summary and the counts (no rows).

fields.description: Row fields to keep (for example ["id","param","value"]); omit for all fields.

commands.title: Batch-set instance or type parameters of up to 500 elements from data: items pick elements by id, ids or a selector (category, name, level, tag) and give params {name: value} with explicit units (mm, m, deg, number, int, bool, text, elementid by name). Never creates parameters; refuses read-only and critical built-in ones (type, workset, phase, level, host) with a reason per element. Run revit_get_parameters first to see names, units and what is writable. Write tool: needs an approved plan; one transaction per element; every value is read back; returns old and new values and a revert list; rolls back on failure unless on_error is skip.

items.description: What to write (500 elements per call in total): each item picks elements with exactly one of id, ids or selector and gives the values.

selector.description: Pick elements by properties instead of ids. Needs category or tag, so the whole model is never scanned; name and level narrow it.

category.description: Category name, for example Walls, Doors, Windows, Pipes or OST_GenericModel.

name.description: Exact element name (for a family instance this is its type name).

level.description: Exact name of the level the element is on.

tag.description: Prefix of the Comments parameter that marks the elements of one build phase.

scope.description: instance (default): the selected element itself (a type id also means that type). type: the element type of each selected element; instances that share a type count once.

params.description: Parameter name -> new value (1 to 50 per item). Each value is either a plain value (true/false = Yes/No, text = text, a whole number = integer) or an object {value, unit}. unit is mm or m (length), deg (angle), number (any other number parameter, in Revit internal units), int, bool, text, or elementid (value is the name or integer id of an element, for example a material). A number parameter always needs a unit.

additionalProperties.description: The new value. Each value is either a plain value (true/false = Yes/No, text = text, a whole number = integer) or an object {value, unit}. unit is mm or m (length), deg (angle), number (any other number parameter, in Revit internal units), int, bool, text, or elementid (value is the name or integer id of an element, for example a material). A number parameter always needs a unit.

value.description: The value itself: number, true/false or text.

unit.description: How to read value: mm, m, deg, number, int, bool, text or elementid.

on_error.description: abort (default): any refused element or failed write changes nothing at all. skip: refused and failed elements are left alone and listed; the others are written.

dry_run.description: Default false. true: do the whole call inside Revit exactly as normal (same checks, same read-back), then roll everything back. The result says dry_run true, committed false and what would change; changed_ids stays empty. Still needs an approved plan like any write.
